candidates.statement: An IVPT study may be used to assess the rate and extent to which a drug (i.e., an active 62 ingredient) from a topical product becomes available at or near a site of action in the skin, and 63 may be used to characterize and compare the rate and extent of bioavailability for a drug from a 64 test topical product and RS. The IVPT flux profiles resemble pharmacokinetic profiles and can 65 be analyzed using unique IVPT endpoints that are somewhat analogous to the pharmacokinetic 66 endpoints of maximum concentration (Cmax) and the area under the concentration-time curve 67 (AUC). Yet, IVPT studies characterize the rate and extent of absorption, not the distribution, 68 metabolism and excretion that occurs in vivo. Therefore, while it is relevant to characterize the 69 kinetics of topical drug bioavailability monitored by IVPT studies, the use in this guidance of the 70 term “cutaneous pharmacokinetics” should not be construed to embody all aspects of 71 pharmacokinetics—only those related to the absorption component that directly controls the rate 72 and extent to which a topically applied drug becomes available locally at the site of action. This 73 guidance focuses on general considerations and recommendations for the method development, 74 method validation, and conduct of IVPT studies that are submitted in ANDAs and intended to 75 support a demonstration of BE. 11

The 444 purpose of the pilot study is to validate the suitability of the selected IVPT method parameters by 445 demonstrating that the performance characteristics of the IVPT method are appropriate to 446 compare the cutaneous pharmacokinetics of a drug delivered topically from a test product and 447 RS. The results from the pilot study, thereby, support the systematic validation of the IVPT 448 method, which proceeds as a distinct study phase following IVPT method development. 449

In addition to the test topical product and 452 RS evaluated in the pilot study, a parallel assessment should be performed with a third topical 453 product or formulation that is known or designed to be different from the RS, to validate the 454 selectivity of the IVPT method to discriminate differences in bioavailability. The IVPT pilot 455 study results should be plotted with error bars, comparing the permeation profiles for the three 456 treatment groups in the pilot study.
